rules.rule: GFC frontend review. File real bugs introduced or directly worsened by the diff: crashes, wrong data shown to users, broken forecast/monitor/verify behavior, auth/premium-gate bypasses, security issues, plus React 19 correctness (stale closures, wrong hook deps, setState during render), Redux/Immer misuse, OpenLayers mistakes (projection, layer leaks, unremoved listeners), and null/undefined derefs on weather data with evidence in the diff. Mark minor-impact items low rather than suppressing them, but require the same evidence (file, line, diff evidence, concrete user impact) at every severity; do not file claims you cannot evidence. Do NOT propose new features, abstractions, refactors, or follow-up work. Do NOT expand to untouched code or hypothetical edge cases without evidence in this diff. Max 10 findings per PR, most severe first. Each finding needs file, line, evidence in the diff, and concrete user impact.

GFC component review. File real bugs in the diff that break rendering, input, or user understanding: crashes, broken controls, inaccessible critical actions with no workaround, wrong copy that causes user error, controlled/uncontrolled input mistakes, responsive breakage on realistic screens. Mark polish-level items low rather than suppressing them. No style taste, no memoization/render micro-opts unless they cause visible breakage, no new-feature ideas. Do not expand to untouched components. Max 10 findings per PR.

GFC backend review. File real bugs in touched routes: missing auth checks, injection, secret/PII leaks, unvalidated client payloads that cause crashes or bad writes, broken Stripe webhook verification, error paths that leak internals or silently fail user-visible operations. Mark minor items low rather than suppressing them. No style nits, no refactor proposals, no speculative hardening without evidence. Treat auth, injection, or secret-handling gaps as critical. Each finding needs file, line, evidence, and user impact.

GFC automation review. File bugs that break the script on realistic inputs: shell injection via PR titles/branch names, wrong gh api usage that fails, missing pagination that drops data, stale-SHA races, secrets leaking into logs. Mark minor robustness items low rather than suppressing them. No style preaching, no feature suggestions.

GFC workflow review. File real safety and correctness bugs: execution of untrusted PR code via pull_request_target checkout, unpinned third-party actions on non-immutable refs, permissions wider than the job needs, secrets from anywhere but secrets context or echoed to logs, concurrency groups that cancel the parallel reviewer, missing timeouts on network-dependent jobs. Mark hygiene items low rather than suppressing them. Critical only for genuine execution/privilege-escalation risks.
Docs review. Flag docs the diff leaves factually wrong (stale instructions, wrong commands, broken links, confusing wording in touched docs). No prose taste, no rewrite suggestions.
